About Me

I am a Physics postgraduate who has completed an M.Phil. in Physics at Government College University Faisalabad. My academic background combines theoretical foundations with experimental research, and my M.Phil. work focused on the structural, dielectric and magnetic characteristics of ferrite/MWCNT nanocomposites.

My research experience has developed my skills in laboratory-based material characterization, experimental data analysis, scientific writing and interpretation of results. I am interested in continuing research in Materials Physics, nanomaterials and functional magnetic materials.

Thesis Title

EXPLORING THE STRUCTURAL, DIELECTRICAL AND MAGNETIC CHARACTERISTICS OF Mg0.5Zn0.5Fe2O4/MWCNTs COMPOSITES SYNTHESIZED BY SOL-GEL AUTO COMBUSTION METHOD.

The research investigated Mg0.5Zn0.5Fe2O4 ferrite composites incorporating multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs), with attention to structural, dielectric/electrical and magnetic characteristics.

Research Objectives

  • Synthesize ferrite nanoparticles and ferrite/MWCNT composite materials using the sol-gel auto-combustion method.
  • Examine structural and bonding characteristics using materials-characterization techniques.
  • Study dielectric and electrical behaviour, including frequency-dependent measurements where applicable.
  • Investigate magnetic parameters such as saturation magnetization, coercivity and retentivity.
  • Analyse experimental results and relate observed material properties to the composition of the composites.

Research Methodology and Characterization

  • Synthesis and processing: sol-gel auto-combustion method and preparation of ferrite/MWCNT composites.
  • Structural characterization: X-ray Diffraction (XRD), including phase identification and crystallite/lattice analysis.
  • Spectroscopic and morphological characterization: FTIR, Raman spectroscopy, UV-Visible spectroscopy, and SEM/TEM techniques.
  • Dielectric/electrical measurements: LCR measurements, dielectric parameters, AC conductivity and impedance analysis.
  • Magnetic characterization: Vibrating Sample Magnetometer (VSM) measurements for magnetic parameters.
  • Data work: graph plotting, interpretation, and scientific reporting using Origin, MATLAB and Excel.

Research and Technical Skills

  • Materials research: ferrite nanoparticles and ferrite/MWCNT composites.
  • Data and computing: Origin, MATLAB, Excel, Python, C++, and intermediate knowledge of C, C++ and MATLAB.
  • Instrumentation: oscilloscope, multimeter, and LCR meter.
  • Research practice: literature review, data interpretation, scientific report/thesis writing, research presentations, and laboratory safety.

Research Experience

Laboratory and Experimental Research Experience: Conducted experimental research on Mg0.5Zn0.5Fe2O4/MWCNT composites prepared using the sol-gel auto-combustion method. Worked with characterization techniques and analysed structural, dielectric and magnetic properties. Interpreted experimental data and prepared scientific reports concerning nanomaterials and their potential applications.

Proposed PhD Research Interests

My intended doctoral research direction is closely connected to my M.Phil. work, where I studied the structural, dielectric and magnetic characteristics of Mg0.5Zn0.5Fe2O4/MWCNTs composites synthesized by the sol-gel auto-combustion method. For my PhD, I plan to focus on ferrite-based nanocomposites and other functional nanomaterials. A key theme will be understanding how composition and material structure, including cation substitution, filler content, particle size and microstructure, influence dielectric, electrical and magnetic properties. I also aim to use advanced characterization techniques such as XRD, electron microscopy, impedance spectroscopy and magnetic measurements to link synthesis conditions with structure and properties. Through this work, I hope to explore the potential of these materials for functional applications such as high-frequency electronics, electromagnetic shielding and microwave absorption. This is a proposed direction based on my existing research background, and the final topic can be adapted to the research interests and official requirements of the selected Russian university and research group.
